newsitem.title: USA: "Decent" chance of more US Sikorsky orders - Dodd.
newsitem.headline: "Decent" chance of more US Sikorsky orders - Dodd.

text.p: There is a "decent" chance that Congress will appropriate more funds for the Pentagon to purchase Black Hawk helicopters built by United Technologies Corp unit Sikorsky Aircraft in the 1998 defense budget, Connecticut Democratic U.S. Senator Chris Dodd said on Wednesday.

"I think we've got a decent chance," Dodd told reporters. "It's nothing locked in concrete, obviously. But we've got a good argument; we've got a united delegation; we're going to have support from the National Guard, which is very important."
"It's an uphill climb," Dodd said. "We think it will be hard, but we think we can win."
The Connecticut congressional delegation and Sikorsky are seeking 18 additional Black Hawks in the federal budget.
President Bill Clinton on Feb. 6 proposed only 18 Black Hawks -- half the number Sikorsky was expecting -- for $246 million.
Connecticut U.S. Democratic Senator Joe Lieberman said on Feb 6 that Sikorsky could lose up to 1,000 jobs unless the number of Black Hawks were increased.
Sikorsky President Eugene Buckley on Wednesday called the proposed cuts "a terrible situation that's developed in the president's budget."
"We're going to fight to get those Black Hawks back," Buckley said in a speech to employees and reporters.
Dodd said Clinton owed him a favor and he would "fight tooth and nail to restore these 18 helicopters."
"This is an issue that goes beyond southwestern Connecticut and Sikorsky," Dodd told Sikorsky employees. He said it was a matter of "national security" to beef up the helicopter budget.
"I happen to think that fellow in the White House owes me a little bit, and so we're going to say to him, 'Get on our side here,'" Dodd said.
Dodd told Reuters it wasn't clear how many Sikorsky jobs were in danger. "So much depends upon foreign sales and other issues," he said.

Buckley told Reuters that there would be a "substantial impact" on Sikorsky's workforce size if the number of Black Hawks were not increased. But he declined to speculate on the likely number of layoffs. About 7,800 of Sikorsky's 8,600 worldwide employees are in Connecticut.

"I am very confident (of increased Black Hawk orders)," Buckley said. "These airplanes are used for medical evacuation; they're used for both civil and military purposes. Therefore, they can help the population in disaster relief."
"These units basically go to the National Guard," he said.
